goal: The admin's rail, store menu, account menus and list rows fetch a link's page when the pointer, a touch or the keyboard focus reaches it, not when it comes into view, through one AdminLink built on a small PolicyLink.
why: Today an admin screen makes 23 to 46 router prefetch requests at rest (28 on the store home, 8 for product editors on a four-row product list), and about 25 again after every save, to fetch nearly the same loading skeleton twelve times. After: 0 on the admin home, 0 for product editors on the list, and at most 2 after hovering one rail link.

commits.title: PolicyLink and AdminLink: a link fetched when it is pointed at

changes.how: First line "use client";. Imports only: `import Link from "next/link";` and from react `useState, type ComponentProps`. Export `type LinkPolicy = "view" | "intent" | "none";` and `export function PolicyLink({ policy, onPointerEnter, onTouchStart, onFocus, ...rest }: Omit<ComponentProps<typeof Link>, "prefetch"> & { policy: LinkPolicy })`. Inside: `const [asked, setAsked] = useState(false);` and render `<Link {...rest} prefetch={policy === "view" || (policy === "intent" && asked) ? null : false} onPointerEnter={(event) => { setAsked(true); onPointerEnter?.(event); }} onTouchStart={(event) => { setAsked(true); onTouchStart?.(event); }} onFocus={(event) => { setAsked(true); onFocus?.(event); }} />`. `null` is Next's default (fetch when in view), so once asked the link in view is fetched at once. Children pass through untouched, so a server component can draw icons, counts and <LinkPending /> inside it, and useLinkStatus() still works because the child sits inside next/link's Link. Doc comment: 'A link with a written prefetch policy (bloat review step 0.13): view (Next's default, when it scrolls into view), intent (when the pointer, a touch or focus reaches it: Next's hover pattern), none (never; for a link that leaves its root layout or opens a file). Step 2.6 uses it on the storefront.'

First line "use client";. `import { PolicyLink, type LinkPolicy } from "@/components/policy-link";` and `import type { ComponentProps } from "react";` and `import type Link from "next/link";`. Export `type AdminLinkProps = Omit<ComponentProps<typeof Link>, "prefetch"> & { policy?: LinkPolicy; /** As next/link's: false means policy none. Kept so a caller's prefetch={false} still type-checks. */ prefetch?: false };` and `export function AdminLink({ policy, prefetch, ...rest }: AdminLinkProps) { return <PolicyLink policy={policy ?? (prefetch === false ? "none" : "intent")} {...rest} />; }`. Doc comment: 'The admin's link: fetched on intent unless a policy is given. The rail, the menus and the list primitives use it, so an admin screen at rest prefetches nothing.'
Add the line `export { AdminLink, type AdminLinkProps } from "./link";`.

do_not: Do not set `export const prefetch = 'force-disabled'` (or any prefetch segment config) on an admin layout, and do not turn on partialPrefetching in next.config.ts: both change every link at once and are other steps' questions.
Do not use PolicyLink on the storefront in this step: step 2.6 does, with its own budgets.
Do not remove LinkPending or move it outside the link: useLinkStatus() only works inside next/link's Link.
Do not drop role="menuitem", aria-current, aria-label or a key while replacing a tag.
Do not convert every raw <Link> in the admin (there are about 950): only the files named. The remaining rows of other lists stay at their recorded counts in the spec and move later.
Do not give View store, a print link or the capacity CSV a policy other than none.
Do not raise a count in the spec's table, and do not widen 'at most 2 after a hover'.
Do not add a bypass to sign-in for the spec; it signs in through auth.setup.ts's saved states.
stop_if: After the change the admin home still makes router prefetch requests at rest: print their paths, find which component draws those links (it is one this brief did not name), and report it before converting more files.

ButtonLink's callers stop type-checking because one passes prefetch={true} or "auto": report the caller.
